site.name: LoseWeight.net
site.tagline: Calculate a realistic, evidence-based path to your goal weight.
site.description: Free calculators and clinician-reviewed guides that show you a realistic timeline, calorie range, and weekly milestones for reaching your goal weight.

home.heroTitle: How long will it actually take?
home.heroBody: Enter your age, height, weight, activity level, and goal. You get a calorie range, a week-by-week timeline, and a projection that slows down as you get lighter, the way real weight loss does.
home.privacyNote: Your measurements stay in your browser. Nothing is sent to us unless you choose to save a plan.
home.whyTitle: Most calculators give you a date you will miss
home.whyBody: The common approach divides the weight you want to lose by a fixed weekly rate, or uses the old rule that 3,500 calories equals one pound. Both assume your body burns the same energy at 90 kg as it does at 75 kg. It doesn't. As you get lighter, your daily expenditure falls, so the same intake produces a smaller deficit and progress slows.
home.whyBody2: This planner recalculates your expenditure every simulated week and shows you the curve instead of the straight line. You can see the difference between the two estimates on your own numbers.
home.toolsBody: Each one runs in your browser and shows its working.
home.guidesBody: Written to be useful on the day you read them, with sources attached to the claims they support.
home.noGuides: No guides have been published in this language yet.
home.trustTitle: What this site does not do
home.trustBody: It does not diagnose you, recommend a medication, or replace a clinician. It gives you arithmetic you can check and explanations you can act on. Where evidence is uncertain, the pages say so.

planner.title: Weight loss planner
planner.intro: Fill in five fields. You get a calorie target, a realistic date, and the week-by-week curve behind it.
planner.sexNote: Used only for the metabolic rate equation, which is sex-specific.
planner.chartNote: The straight line is what a fixed-rate calculator would tell you. The curve accounts for the fact that a lighter body burns less.
planner.milestoneHealthy: Top of the healthy BMI range
planner.goalTooLow: That goal is below the healthy BMI range for your height ({min}). Consider setting a goal inside the range, or talk to a clinician first.
planner.goalAboveCurrent: Your goal weight is above your current weight. This planner is built for weight loss.
planner.clampedFloor: Your requested rate would put you below {floor} calories a day, which is the lowest we will suggest without medical supervision. The plan uses {floor} instead, so it will take longer than the rate you picked.
planner.clampedDeficit: Your requested rate needs a deficit larger than 25% of your maintenance. Larger deficits cost more lean tissue and are harder to sustain, so the plan uses a 25% deficit instead.
planner.plateauNote: On this intake, weight loss flattens out around {weight} before reaching your goal. To go further you would need to lower intake again or add activity, and recalculate at that point.
planner.assumptions: Predictive equations carry real error. Your actual maintenance may sit 10 to 15% either side of the estimate. Treat the number as week one's experiment: track your weight for three weeks, compare the trend against the projection, then adjust by 100 to 200 calories.
planner.savedNote: Saved in this browser only. There is no account and no sync.
planner.saveFailed: Could not save. Your browser may be blocking storage or out of space.
planner.firstWeekIntro: Change nothing else while you gather a baseline. The point of these three weeks is to find out what your body actually does at this intake, not to make progress fast.
planner.fwWeighValue: Daily, same conditions, read the 7 day average only
planner.fwDontChange: Do not change your calorie target before that date, whatever the scale does in week one.
planner.scenarioGentleTradeoff: Easiest to sustain and protects muscle best. Slowest, so it needs patience.
planner.scenarioStandardTradeoff: The usual balance of speed and adherence for most people.
planner.scenarioFasterTradeoff: Fastest on paper. More hunger, more lean tissue lost, and the hardest to hold through a bad week.
planner.scenarioNotFor: Less suitable if you train hard, are already lean, or have a history of restrictive eating.
planner.rangeNote: Shown as a range because the underlying equation is an estimate, not a measurement.
planner.scenarioCapped: Capped at the safe limit, so this is the same as Standard

tracker.title: Progress tracker
tracker.intro: Log your weight and read the 7 day average, not the daily number. Day to day swings of 1 to 2 kg come from water, food in transit, and sodium, and they are larger than a week of real fat loss.
tracker.noEntries: No weigh-ins yet. Add your first one to start the trend line.
tracker.localOnly: Your weigh-ins are saved in this browser only. Clearing site data or switching device loses them, so export a backup now and then.
tracker.needThreeWeeks: Add three weeks of weigh-ins to get a reliable read on your rate.
tracker.plateauNone: Your 7 day average is still moving down. Nothing to fix.
tracker.plateauShort: Your average has been flat for {weeks} weeks. That is still within normal fluctuation. A plateau needs three or more flat weeks before it means anything.
tracker.plateauReal: Your average has been flat for {weeks} weeks. That qualifies as a plateau. The usual cause is that your maintenance fell as you lost weight, so recalculate your plan at your current weight before cutting calories further.
tracker.backupHint: There is no account and no cloud sync. The export file is your backup.
tracker.noPlan: You have not saved a plan yet.
tracker.importEmpty: No usable rows found in that file.
tracker.chartSummary: Weight trend from {start} to {end}. Started at {startWeight}, latest 7 day average {latest}, change {change}.
tracker.invalidWeight: Enter a weight between 20 and 500 kg.
tracker.invalidDate: Pick a date that is not in the future.

calculators.title: Calculators
calculators.intro: Each calculator runs in your browser and shows the formula it used.
calculators.tdeeDesc: What your body burns in a day, broken into resting rate and movement.
calculators.bmiDesc: Your BMI, what the category means, and the weight range it maps to at your height.
calculators.whtrDesc: A better predictor of individual risk than BMI, and it needs only a tape measure.
calculators.proteinDesc: How much protein protects lean mass in a deficit, and how much fiber fits your intake.
calculators.plateauDesc: Check whether a stall is a real plateau or normal fluctuation, and what to change first.
calculators.waistHelp: Measure at the midpoint between your lowest rib and the top of your hip bone, at the end of a normal breath out. Keep the tape snug without compressing the skin.
calculators.bodyFatHelp: If you know it from a DEXA scan, the calculator uses the Katch-McArdle equation instead, which is more accurate.
calculators.weeksFlat: Weeks with no change in your 7 day average
calculators.plateauNeedsData: This reads the weigh-ins you have saved in the tracker on this device. Add a few weeks of entries and come back.
calculators.vInsufficientWhy: You have {days} days of weigh-ins. Three weeks is the minimum before a flat stretch means anything, because daily swings are larger than a week of fat loss.
calculators.vSparse: Too few weigh-ins to read a trend
calculators.vSparseWhy: You are averaging {perWeek} weigh-ins a week over {days} days. A 7 day average needs at least three or four readings a week to be stable. Weigh more often before drawing conclusions.
calculators.vOnTrackWhy: Your 7 day average is falling at about {rate} a week. Nothing needs changing.
calculators.vNormalWhy: Your average has been flat for {weeks} week or so. That is inside normal water and gut-content variation. Wait until you have three or more flat weeks.
calculators.vSlowerWhy: You are losing about {rate} a week against a plan of {planned}. That is still progress, so the first thing to check is measurement, not calories.
calculators.vPlateauWhy: Your average has not moved for {weeks} weeks with consistent weighing. The usual cause is that your maintenance fell as you lost weight.
calculators.stepData: Confirm the data first. Weigh daily under the same conditions and read only the 7 day average.
calculators.stepMeasure: Weigh your food for one week instead of estimating. Reported intake drifts upward over months and you cannot see it from the inside.
calculators.stepActivity: Check whether your daily movement has dropped. It usually does in a deficit, without you deciding to.
calculators.stepRecalc: Recalculate your energy needs at your current weight, not your starting weight. For you that is about {maintenance} calories.
calculators.stepAdjust: Only then consider 100 to 150 fewer calories, and give it two weeks.
calculators.stepProfessional: If the stall persists past that, or you are losing hair, sleeping badly, or your period has stopped, speak to a clinician rather than cutting further.
calculators.contextHint: These do not change the numbers. They change how much confidence to put in them.
calculators.ctxCycle: I menstruate and could be in the second half of my cycle
calculators.ctxIllness: Recent illness, travel, or a big change in routine
calculators.ctxSodium: Noticeably saltier food than usual in the last few days
calculators.ctxTraining: Started or increased resistance training recently
calculators.ctxNote: Water retention from any of these can hide two to three weeks of real fat loss. It is worth waiting another two weeks before changing anything.

guides.title: Guides
guides.intro: Written to answer the question you came with. Sources are attached to the claims they support.
guides.notReviewed: This guide is written by {name} but has not yet completed his medical accuracy review. It is based on the sources listed at the end. Check anything affecting your treatment with your own doctor.
guides.empty: No guides have been published in this language yet.
guides.emptyNote: Guides on LoseWeight.net are written separately for each language rather than machine translated, so a guide written in another language will not appear here.
guides.reviewedSelf: Written and reviewed for medical accuracy by {name}, a physician educated at Azerbaijan Medical University with a professional background in pediatrics in Azerbaijan. He is not licensed to practice medicine in the United States.
